evidence.quote: Let $M^n$ be a closed connected oriented smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge2$. If $M$ admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive scalar curvature, then $$(c_M)_*[M]=0\qquad\text{in }H_n(B\pi_1(M);\mathbb Q).$$

Suppose $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_M\ge\kappa>0$. On the above bundle $Z$, let $G:Z\to\mathbb R^q$ be smooth and bounded with all mixed derivatives bounded, and suppose $L_0>0$ and $$\sup_{1\le i\le q}\abs{d_{\widetilde M}G_i}\le L_0,
 \qquad q\ge2.$$ There is a constant $C_n$ depending only on $n$ such that, if $$\label{eq:shortening-smallness}
 C_n(2+\log q)L_0^2\le\kappa/4,$$ then for every finite integer $k\ge1$ there are a complete stabilized metric $$\mathfrak g_k=h_k+\sum_{\nu=1}^{kq}m_{k,\nu}^2d\theta_\nu^2
 \quad\text{on }Z\times\mathbb T^{kq}$$ and a smooth bounded map $G^{(k)}:Z\to\mathbb R^q$ satisfying $$\label{eq:shortening-output}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\mathfrak g_k}\ge\kappa/2,\qquad
 \norm{G^{(k)}-G}_{\infty}<\pi/10,\qquad
 \abs{dG^{(k)}}_{\rm op}\le\sqrt{q+1}\,4^{-k}L_0.$$ The infinity norm in the middle inequality is the target coordinate maximum, followed by the supremum over $Z$. All metric coefficients, warps, and maps have uniform bounds of every order at each fixed finite stage; their equivalence and derivative constants may depend on that stage.

outputs.exact_statement: Let $M^n$ be a closed connected oriented smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge2$. If $M$ admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive scalar curvature, then $$(c_M)_*[M]=0\qquad\text{in }H_n(B\pi_1(M);\mathbb Q).$$
No closed smooth aspherical manifold, whether orientable or not, admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive scalar curvature.
Let $g$ be a Riemannian metric of nonnegative scalar curvature on a closed smooth aspherical manifold $M$, not necessarily oriented. Then $g$ is flat.

Let $M^n$ and $N^n$ be closed connected oriented smooth manifolds of dimension $n\ge2$, with $N$ aspherical. If a continuous map $f:M\to N$ has nonzero ordinary oriented degree $d\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, then $M$ admits no Riemannian metric whose scalar curvature is strictly positive everywhere.*

*In particular, if $P^n$ is any closed connected oriented smooth manifold, the oriented connected sum $N\#P$ admits no such metric.
Every closed oriented smooth manifold of positive dimension admitting a Riemannian metric of nonnegative scalar curvature has zero real simplicial volume.
If a closed connected oriented manifold $M^n$ has positive real simplicial volume, then $(c_M)_*[M]\ne0$ in $H_n(B\Gamma;\mathbb Q)$.

Let $M$ be closed and connected, not necessarily oriented, and suppose that $g$ has nonnegative scalar curvature. Either $M$ admits a metric of strictly positive scalar curvature, or $g$ is Ricci-flat. In the Ricci-flat case, if $M$ is oriented and has positive dimension, then $\|M\|=0$.

There are $s\ge1$, $H<\infty$, a smooth equivariant probability map $h:\widetilde M\to\mathcal K_s$, and an equivariant simplicial map $h_0:\widetilde M\to\mathcal K_s$ such that*

1.  *the coordinate functions of $h$ are smooth and locally supported on finitely many labels, and $\abs{dh}_{\ell^1}\le H$;*

2.  *$h$ and $h_0$ are joined by an equivariant homotopy that is proper as a map $\widetilde M\times[0,1]\to\mathcal K_s$;*

3.  *there is an invariant alternating homogeneous rational group $n$-cocycle $\omega$ whose evaluation on the labelled fundamental simplices of $M$ is nonzero.

Put $v_0=\dim\mathcal O_L$. There are a closed oriented smooth $d$-manifold $C$, with $d\le2v_0+2$, a principal left $\Gamma$-cover $\widehat C\to C$, and equivariant maps $$\mathcal O_L\xrightarrow{i}\widehat C
 \xrightarrow{r}\mathcal K_L,
 \qquad r i=\pi.$$ Moreover $v_0\le\abs{B_\Gamma(1,L)}$.

One can triangulate $C$ so finely that the lifted triangulation has the following properties:*

1.  *the union of the supports of $r(o)$ over any closed primal simplex has diameter at most $2L$;*

2.  *there is an augmentation-preserving equivariant chain map $$\mathcal F:C_*(\mathcal O_L)\longrightarrow
     C_*^{\mathrm{dual}}(\widehat C)$$ with finite output, such that if a dual cell to a primal simplex $\tau$ occurs in $\mathcal F(e)$, then every label of every $r(o)$, $o\in\tau$, is within $2L$ of every vertex of $e$.

There are a compact set $K_*\subset D_L$ and a class $$u\in H^{n+d}(D_L,D_L\setminus K_*;\mathbb Q)$$ such that*

1.  *if $[t,o]\in K_*$, every label of $t$ is within $7L$ of every label of $r(o)$;*


2.  *the compactly supported evaluation $$\label{eq:compact-pairing-nonzero}
     \ip{\Phi_h^*u,[X]_{\mathrm{lf}}}\ne0$$ is nonzero.*

*Here $[X]_{\mathrm{lf}}$ is the locally finite fundamental class.

The map $V:D_L\to\mathbb R^q$ has the following properties.*

1.  *It is continuous and proper, and $\norm{V}_{p_R}\le24L$ on $K_*$.*

2.  *If $t,t'\in\mathcal K_s$ satisfy $$\max\{\norm{V_o(t)}_\infty,\norm{V_o(t')}_\infty\}\le110L,
     \qquad
     \norm{V_o(t)-V_o(t')}_\infty\le14R,$$ then the union of their supports has diameter at most $L$.*

3.  *The map $\mathcal V=V\Phi_h:X\to\mathbb R^q$ is smooth. With $K_0=sH$, each of its rows satisfies $$\sup_X\abs{d_{\widetilde M}\mathcal V_i}\le K_0,$$ where $K_0$ is independent of $R$.

There is a compact oriented smooth $(q-n)$-manifold $A_+$ with boundary, together with a smooth map $$(o_0,y_0):A_+\longrightarrow C\times\mathbb R^q,$$ such that $\norm{y_0}_{p_R}<T_0$ everywhere, $\rho(o_0,y_0)>4R$ on $\partial A_+$, and its intersections with $j:N\to C\times\mathbb R^q$ are transverse, interior, and have nonzero total oriented count. The component maps may be taken constant in the inward collar coordinate near $\partial A_+$.

Suppose that, in the reference charts, a scalar operator has the form $$L\xi=-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j\xi+b^i\partial_i\xi+c\xi,$$ with uniformly $C^{0,\alpha}$ coefficients, uniformly bounded drift, uniformly positive definite principal matrix, and $c\ge c_0>0$. Then $$L:C_b^{2,\alpha}(B)\longrightarrow C_b^{0,\alpha}(B)$$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is bounded in terms of the indicated uniform bounds. If the coefficients have bounded derivatives of every order, the inverse also maps $C_b^{j,\alpha}$ boundedly into $C_b^{j+2,\alpha}$ for every $j\ge0$.

Let $(B,g)$ be uniformly controlled as above, and let $\ell\in C_b^\infty(B)$. Fix $\varepsilon,w,B_0,s>0$ and $0\le\beta<1$. Suppose $N$ is smooth, positive, nondecreasing, constant near zero, and equal to $1$ for $t\ge1/2$. Define the quantities in [eq:graph-quantities] and $$\lambda(r)=B_0(r^2+s^2)^{\beta/2}.$$ There is a unique solution in the uniform $C^{2,\alpha}$ class with a uniform band margin to $$\label{eq:graph-equation} -\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g U =\lambda(r)\tan\left(\frac{\ell-\varepsilon f}{w}\right), \qquad \abs{\ell-\varepsilon f}<\frac{\pi w}{2}.$$ This solution lies in $C_b^\infty(B)$, and the band has a positive uniform margin. The metric [eq:graph-metric-update] is uniformly controlled and complete.* *The solution is invariant under every isometry preserving the equation’s data. The following parameter statement will be used below. Fix the reference cover, its metric and nested charts, and the equation parameters $\varepsilon,w,B_0,s,\beta,N$. Let $(g_a,\ell_a)$ be a jointly smooth family over a finite-dimensional parameter manifold $A$. For every relatively compact subset $V'\Subset V$ of a parameter chart, assume common constants $c_{V'},C_{V'}>0$ such that $$c_{V'}g_{\rm ref}\le g_a\le C_{V'}g_{\rm ref}\qquad(a\in V'),$$ and common bounds in the fixed reference charts for every mixed derivative of the coefficients of $g_a$ and of $\ell_a$, including order zero. Then $a\mapsto f_a$ is smooth in every $C_b^{j,\alpha}$ norm, for $j\ge0$ and $0<\alpha<1$. If $A$ is compact, all mixed derivatives of $f_a$ are uniformly bounded and the tangent band has a common positive margin. For a bundle of such covers, the local solutions glue whenever fixed reference deck transformations carry one local data set to another.

Fix a finite-stage smooth family of metrics of the form [eq:fibre-stabilized-metric], equivariant under the flat transition maps over the closed manifold $A$, with all mixed derivatives bounded and uniform equivalence to a reference product. For any fixed metric $g_A$ on $A$, set $$g_P=g_h+P^2g_A+\sum_{ u=1}^b m_ u^2d heta_ u^2 \quad ext{on }Z imes\mathbb T^b,$$ using the flat splitting and no mixed parameter terms. As $P o\infty$, $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{g_P}$ converges uniformly to the scalar curvature of the fibre metrics. If $H:Z o\mathbb R^q$ has bounded mixed derivatives, its differential in the parameter directions has norm tending uniformly to zero. Each $g_P$ is complete and uniformly controlled.

Suppose $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_M\ge\kappa>0$. On the above bundle $Z$, let $G:Z\to\mathbb R^q$ be smooth and bounded with all mixed derivatives bounded, and suppose $L_0>0$ and $$\sup_{1\le i\le q}\abs{d_{\widetilde M}G_i}\le L_0,
 \qquad q\ge2.$$ There is a constant $C_n$ depending only on $n$ such that, if $$\label{eq:shortening-smallness}
 C_n(2+\log q)L_0^2\le\kappa/4,$$ then for every finite integer $k\ge1$ there are a complete stabilized metric $$\mathfrak g_k=h_k+\sum_{\nu=1}^{kq}m_{k,\nu}^2d\theta_\nu^2
 \quad\text{on }Z\times\mathbb T^{kq}$$ and a smooth bounded map $G^{(k)}:Z\to\mathbb R^q$ satisfying $$\label{eq:shortening-output}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\mathfrak g_k}\ge\kappa/2,\qquad
 \norm{G^{(k)}-G}_{\infty}<\pi/10,\qquad
 \abs{dG^{(k)}}_{\rm op}\le\sqrt{q+1}\,4^{-k}L_0.$$ The infinity norm in the middle inequality is the target coordinate maximum, followed by the supremum over $Z$. All metric coefficients, warps, and maps have uniform bounds of every order at each fixed finite stage; their equivalence and derivative constants may depend on that stage.

Assume $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_M\ge\kappa>0$ and take the comparison data of 8 at scale $R$, so that $$L_0=J/R,\qquad \log q\le JR.$$ For all sufficiently large $R$, fix these data once and for all. Then for every finite $k\ge1$ there is a stabilized metric $\mathfrak g_k$ on $Z\times\mathbb T^{kq}$ with scalar curvature at least $\kappa/2$, and a smooth map $$F_k:Z\longrightarrow S^q$$ equal to a single value outside a compact set, with nonzero degree, such that $$\label{eq:stabilized-contraction-bound} \abs{dF_k}_{\rm op}\le C(q)4^{-k}J/R.$$ The sphere has its standard unit metric. The constant $C(q)$ is independent of $k$. If desired, the circle lengths may be increased so that the projection to the standard $\mathbb T^{kq}$ also has operator norm at most $4^{-k}J/R$; this does not change scalar curvature or the bound on $dF_k$.

For every integer $d\geq2$ and every $\chi>0$ there is a number $\delta(d,\chi)>0$ for which the following data do not exist:* 1. *a smooth oriented $d$-manifold $Y$ without boundary, possibly disconnected, with a torus-stabilized metric $\mathcal G$ satisfying $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\mathcal G}\geq\chi$;* 2. *a smooth map $F:Y\to S^d$, equal to one value outside a compact set, such that $\deg F\ne0$ and $\norm{dF}_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\delta(d,\chi)$ everywhere.* *The constant is independent of the finite circle count in [eq:stabilized-metric]. Neither the base metric nor the stabilized metric is assumed complete.
